summary: Lighthouse Point at Beaver Harbour, New Brunswick: the Drews Head light, first lit in 1876, kept by a line of families until 1984, now a Coast Guard tower.

light.fog_signal: fog horn, 6 s blast every 60 s

structures.type: square wooden tower attached to the keeper's dwelling
structures.note: 36 ft (11 m) from base to vane, per Lighthouse Friends. Replaced by a skeletal tower in the late 1960s.
Replaced the original tower and dwelling in the late 1960s (Lighthouse Friends; Rowlett). The sources do not say how long it stood.
White cylindrical tower with red top. CCG List of Lights gives 8.6 m structure height above ground; Rowlett gives 8 m (28 ft).

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed. Walk of about 800 m (1/2 mile) round trip with limited parking at the end of Lighthouse Road (Rowlett).

events.note: Parliament appropriated funds for a lighthouse at Beaver Harbour; a site on Drews Head was chosen that autumn and bought from Lewis Holmes for $100
Station established (Rowlett directory). Lighthouse Friends gives the first lighting in 1876.

Hand fog horn established at Drews Head, to be sounded when vessels' fog signals were heard nearby

Fourth-order lamp installed in the lantern room (Lighthouse Friends; not traced in the Department reports)

corrections.why: Lighthouse Friends dates the inaugural lighting to 15 January 1876. Rowlett gives 1875 as the year the station was established, which is not the same event. The record took the establishment year as the first lighting.

The 1875 tower was wooden and was replaced in the late 1960s. The present cylindrical tower is fiberglass and dates from 1984 (Lighthouse Friends; Rowlett). The record keeps the 1875 tower as the original.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rowlett gives 1875 as the station's establishment year. Lighthouse Friends gives 15 January 1876 as the first lighting of the lamps. Both are kept in the story, and 1876 is proposed as first_lit.
The original light was a fixed white light (Lighthouse Friends; 1905 report). The present light is Iso W 6s (CCG List of Lights). The record's characteristic is the present one.

Present focal height: 14.2 m (CCG) against 14.5 m (47 ft, Rowlett). Present tower: 8.6 m structure height above ground (CCG) against 8 m (28 ft, Rowlett). The original light was 45 ft (13.7 m) above high water (Lighthouse Friends).

notes_for_editor: Sources: Lighthouse Friends is the only source for the keepers before 1900 (no Canadian report before the fiscal year ended June 30, 1900 is in the local corpus), so Munro, Snell and Conley's 1892 start rest on it alone. The Lighthouse Friends roster starts Munro in 1875, but its own text dates his first lighting to 15 January 1876. The 1903 and 1904 keeper lists are OCR'd. Checked on the page images on 2026-10-28: the 1903 row (printed p. 214, scan 227) puts 'Conlev, John C' on the same printed line as 'Drews Head', and the OCR name and station blocks run in the same order with the same count (ten and ten), so the pairing is by row; the spelling is read at screen resolution and may be 'Conley' in print. The 1904 row (printed p. 158, scan 171) puts 'Eldridge, John M' on the same line as 'Drews Head, Beaver Harbour'. The 1905 list has the same Eldridge line (text only, scan 341, printed p. 260). Lighthouse Friends' text says Eldridge 'served as keeper for several years in the early 1900s', while its roster gives 1904 to 1926; the story states both and keeps the roster's dates. The 1915 keeper table in the report (an 'Eldridge, J. M.' with an appointment date of 2 May 1904) and the 1914-15 table of works ('a fourth order dioptric lens') are split into columns by the OCR, so I did not match them to Drews Head; the 1915 fourth-order lamp therefore rests on Lighthouse Friends. The 1876 Harding report is not in the corpus; it is cited only as Lighthouse Friends reports it. No Canadian newspaper archive was reachable. No sourced storm, wreck or rescue at this station was found, so the story has no 'Storms, wrecks and rescues' chapter. No Canadian Register of Historic Places entry was found in search, and no heritage designation is claimed. Wikipedia was read for leads only (its London Gazette citation of 1 February 1876 was not followed). Lighthouse Friends is copyrighted: the story paraphrases it and quotes only short phrases. Photos: the record's Wikimedia Commons photo stands; no new photo was checked. The 1926 to 1928 gap and the 1939 to 1952 gap in the keeper list are unexplained by the sources.
